bull.last: LMT: argues long. Lockheed Martin has demonstrated exceptional operational execution, delivering 52.8% YoY EPS growth and generating $2,626M in quarterly free cash flow, underpinned by robust structural tailwinds after the CEO highlighted permanent Iran War-related demand. Technically, LMT has surged 8.34% over the past 5 days, executing a clean breakout above its 20-day high of 538.10 to trade at 552.09 on elevated volume (vol_ratio of 1.36). Heading into its October 22, 2026 pre-market earnings print (expected EPS of 7.5112), LMT has beaten estimates in 3 of the last 4 quarters, including a 10.5% EPS surprise in the most recent quarter ($7.94 actual vs. $7.1846 expected). Market positioning is decidedly bullish into the event, evidenced by a very low options put/call volume ratio of 0.42 and short interest of just 1.4% of float. While the 200-day SMA at 559.1056 provides immediate resistance, an earnings beat leveraging the options market's 5.37% implied move can readily propel the stock through this level toward analyst targets.

bear.last: LMT: Chasing LMT after an 8.34% 5-day rip directly into major overhead resistance at the 200-day SMA of 559.11 is terrible risk-reward right before the 2026-10-22 pre-market earnings print. The move is severely overbought with a 20-day z-score of 2.83 and an RSI14 of 64.93, triggering an active quantitative mean-reversion short signal. Options market positioning reflects extreme complacency with a put/call volume ratio of just 0.42 despite daily short volume running elevated at 57.6%. Furthermore, Kronos projects a 5-day decline of -1.51% with only a 35% probability of moving higher, while insiders have dumped shares across 9 open-market sales totaling $117,623 with zero buys over the last 90 days. Betting on an earnings blowout when expectations demand $20.69B in revenue and EPS of 7.5112 after the stock already rallied 8.34% leaves longs exposed to severe multiple compression and sell-the-news repricing.
